name: Haggai
sourceNote: Translated from the Hebrew of the Westminster Leningrad Codex (the Masoretic Text). It was checked against the Hebrew Minor Prophets scrolls from Qumran (4QXII, 4QXII-b and -e) and Wadi Murabba‘at (MurXII, early 2nd century AD), whose text is very close to the Masoretic Text. The transcriptions used are Martin Abegg’s, as published in the ETCBC Dead Sea Scrolls dataset. It was also checked against the Septuagint, using Brenton’s public-domain English translation. Portions of Haggai also survive (reportedly) in the Greek Minor Prophets Scroll from Nahal Hever (8HevXIIgr, about the turn of the era), which is a revision of the Septuagint toward the Hebrew. Its readings could not be checked directly, so any that are cited are marked “reported.” Significant differences are footnoted; differences of spelling and damage to the scrolls are not. The divine title YHWH Tseva’ot is translated “Yahweh of Armies” (see the note at 1:2). Dates are given with their approximate modern months; the notes give the original month and, where it is commonly reckoned, the exact date. Verse numbers follow the standard English Bible: in Haggai, English and Hebrew verse numbers are the same.

verses.text: On the first day of the sixth month of King Darius’s second year (in August–September),{a} a message from Yahweh came through the prophet Haggai{b} for Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, who governed Judah, and for the high priest Joshua son of Jehozadak:{c}
“Thus says Yahweh of Armies:{d} This people says, ‘The time has not come, the time for the house of Yahweh to be rebuilt.’”
Then Yahweh’s message came through the prophet Haggai:
“Is it a time for you yourselves to dwell in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?{e}
Now therefore, thus says Yahweh of Armies: Set your heart on your ways.

You have sown much and brought in little; you eat, but never to fullness; you drink, but never to drunkenness; you clothe yourselves, but no one is warm. And he who earns wages earns them for a bag pierced with holes.
“Thus says Yahweh of Armies: Set your heart on your ways.
Go up into the hills, bring timber, and rebuild the house, so I can enjoy it and be honored there, says Yahweh.

You expected a large harvest, but it turned out small; whatever you brought home, I blew away. Why? announces Yahweh of Armies. Because my house remains a ruin, while every one of you hurries off to his own house.
Therefore over you the heavens have held back the dew, and the earth has held back its produce.
I have summoned a drought{f} over the land and the hills, over the grain, the new wine, the oil, whatever the soil produces, over people and livestock, and over everything they work for.”

Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of Yahweh their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, as Yahweh their God had sent him. And the people feared before Yahweh.
Then Haggai, the messenger of Yahweh, spoke to the people with Yahweh’s message,{g} saying, “I am with you, declares Yahweh.”

And Yahweh stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people. And they came and did work on the house of Yahweh of Armies, their God,
on the twenty-fourth day of the month, in the sixth month (in August–September), in the second year of Darius the king.{h}

notes.text: Hebrew “in the sixth month,” that is, Elul, in the calendar whose year begins in the spring. The second year of Darius I (who reigned 522–486 BC) is 520 BC. As the dates are commonly reckoned, this day was about August 29, 520 BC. Because the Hebrew months were lunar, each corresponds to parts of two modern months.
Haggai probably means “festal” (from hag, “feast”). The Septuagint has “Speak to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, of the tribe of Judah.”

Zerubbabel probably means “seed of Babylon”; Shealtiel, “I have asked God”; Joshua, “Yahweh saves” (in Greek, Iēsous, “Jesus”); Jehozadak, “Yahweh is righteous.” Joshua is called Jeshua in Ezra and Nehemiah.

Hebrew YHWH Tseva’ot, traditionally “the LORD of hosts.” The “armies” are the forces of heaven (the angels and the stars) and sometimes the armies of Israel. The title is translated “Yahweh of Armies” throughout.
Hebrew harev, “in ruins.” The same word appears in verse 9.
Hebrew horev, “drought,” plays on harev, “in ruins” (verses 4 and 9): because the house lies in ruins (harev), Yahweh calls a drought (horev).
Or “with Yahweh’s commission.” The word “messenger” (mal’akh) is the same word as in Malachi (“my messenger”).
About September 21, 520 BC. Some scholars attach the date to the beginning of 2:1.

verses.text: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month (in September–October),{a} Yahweh’s message came through the prophet Haggai:{b}
“Speak now to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people, saying,
‘Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? And how do you see it now? Is it not as nothing in your eyes?

Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel, declares Yahweh. Be strong, O Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land, declares Yahweh. Work, for I am with you, declares Yahweh of Armies,
This is the promise I made you when you left Egypt.{c} My Spirit remains among you. Do not be afraid.
“‘For thus says Yahweh of Armies: Yet once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth and the sea and the dry land.{d}
And I will make all nations tremble, and the desirable things of every nation shall come,{e} and I will fill this house with glory, says Yahweh of Armies.
The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, declares Yahweh of Armies.
The latter glory of this house shall be greater than the former, says Yahweh of Armies. And in this place I will give peace, declares Yahweh of Armies.’”{f}
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month (in November–December) of Darius’s second year,{g} Yahweh’s message came to the prophet Haggai:
“Thus says Yahweh of Armies: Ask the priests for a ruling:{h}
‘If a man carries holy meat in the fold of his garment, and with his fold touches bread or pottage or wine or oil or any food, will it be made holy?’” And the priests answered, “No.”
Then Haggai said, “If someone defiled by a corpse touches any of these, will it be defiled?” And the priests answered, “It will be defiled.”
Then Haggai answered and said, “So is this people, and so is this nation before me, declares Yahweh, and so is every work of their hands; and what they offer there is unclean.{i}
“And now, set your heart on it from this day onward.{j} Before stone was laid upon stone in the temple of Yahweh,
how did you fare? When one came to a heap of twenty measures, there were but ten; when one came to the wine vat to draw fifty measures, there were but twenty.{k}
I struck you with blight and with mildew and with hail in all the work of your hands, yet you did not turn to me,{l} declares Yahweh.
Set your heart from this day onward, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month (in November–December), from the day that the foundation of the temple of Yahweh was laid—set your heart on it:
Is the seed yet in the barn? As for the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree, they have borne nothing. From this day on I will bless you.”
And the word of Yahweh came a second time to Haggai on the twenty-fourth day of the month, saying,
“Tell Zerubbabel, governor of Judah: I am about to shake the sky and the earth,
and I will topple royal thrones and break the power of the foreign kingdoms. I will overturn chariots and their drivers; horses and riders will fall, each killed by his comrade’s sword.

On that day, declares Yahweh of Armies, I will take you, O Zerubbabel my servant, the son of Shealtiel, declares Yahweh, and I will make you like a signet ring,{m} for I have chosen you, declares Yahweh of Armies.”

notes.text: Tishri, the seventh month. The twenty-first day was the last day of the Feast of Booths (Leviticus 23:34–36). As commonly reckoned, it was about October 17, 520 BC.
The Wadi Murabba‘at Minor Prophets scroll reads “came to Haggai.”
The Septuagint lacks the first clause, “according to the word that I covenanted with you when you came out of Egypt.”
Quoted in Hebrews 12:26–27. The Septuagint has “Yet once I will shake the heaven, and the earth.”

Or “the desire of all nations shall come.” The Hebrew noun is singular (“desire,” “what is desired”), but the verb is plural, which suggests valued things. The Latin Vulgate’s “the desired one of all nations will come” gave rise to a messianic reading. The Septuagint has “the choice portions of all the nations.”
The Septuagint adds “even peace of soul for a possession to everyone who builds, to raise up this temple.”
About December 18, 520 BC. Kislev is the ninth month.
Hebrew torah, “instruction” or “law.”

The Septuagint adds “and whoever approaches them shall be defiled because of their early burdens; they shall be pained because of their toils; and you have hated him who reproved in the gates” (compare Amos 5:10).
Hebrew “upward,” meaning either “from this day forward” or “backward from this day.” The same expression appears in verse 18.
The measures are not named in the Hebrew. The Septuagint has “twenty measures of barley.” In the second clause, the Hebrew “fifty” is literally “fifty of the winepress” (purah).
Compare Amos 4:9. The Hebrew is literally “yet there was not you to me.” The Septuagint has “yet you did not return to me.”
A signet ring was a royal seal, a sign of authority. This reverses the word against Zerubbabel’s grandfather Jehoiachin (Coniah) in Jeremiah 22:24.
